images.title: Fewer squares in each hundred
images.purpose: Shows the number of perfect squares in each block of 100 from 1 to 1000 as columns of dots, falling from 10 to 1.
images.composition: Plain white background, the main object large and centred with wide empty margins, no scenery, no characters, no extra decoration. Ten columns of dots standing on one baseline, with labels only under the first and last columns.
images.exact_structure: One horizontal baseline with exactly 10 evenly spaced columns of equal round dots, one column per block of 100. From left to right the columns hold exactly 10, 4, 3, 3, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2 and 1 dots, 31 dots in all. The first column is filled teal (#0072B2), the middle eight grey (#6B7280), and the last column's single dot reddish purple (#CC79A7). Under the first column: 1 to 100; above it: 10 squares. Under the last column: 901 to 1000; beside its dot: 961. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Squares get rarer as numbers grow, because the gaps between them keep widening.
images.description: Shows the number of perfect squares in each block of 100 from 1 to 1000 as columns of dots, falling from 10 to 1.
images.context: Counts per hundred: 10, 4, 3, 3, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2, 1; the largest square below 1000 is 31² = 961.

image_decisions.why: Columns of dots shrinking from left to right show the thinning of squares in a single look.
